item.title: Fashola urges grassroots mobilisation ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor and Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola, has urged All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and engage stakeholders across party lines to secure victory in the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the call on Tuesday at a strategic meeting of South-West political stakeholders held in Ikeja, Lagos. The meeting was attended by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, APC State Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, and other party leaders and zonal coordinators. Fashola outlined a strategy for unifying party structures and increasing voter turnout ahead of the elections. He urged participants from the six states in the zone to establish structured stakeholder engagement forums at three levels: state, local government and ward. Emphasising the need for inclusive engagement, he said stakeholders should not be limited to APC members but should include individuals and groups capable of influencing electoral outcomes across party lines. “A stakeholder is anyone who can impact election outcomes, spanning party lines, opposing caucuses, artisans and union members,” he said. Fashola, who is working with former Ondo State Governor Segun Mimiko, former Ekiti State Governor Segun Oni and Secretary Senator Fatai Buhari on the Presidential Campaign Council’s South-West strategy, said he would visit each state after the initial engagement forums had been established. He said the visits would provide opportunities to address local political concerns, respect the peculiarities of each state and escalate issues requiring national intervention. Describing politics as local, Fashola urged party leaders to reach out to newly registered voters and re-engage those who had become apathetic towards the electoral process. He also called on them to recognise the significance of the country’s North-South political rotation and take advantage of the prevailing political moment to strengthen the party’s electoral prospects. The meeting later went into a closed-door session, with a communiqué expected at the end of the deliberations for release to the media. item.title: ‘Uncle Sam, Osoba, others built Daily Times, I’m just a custodian’ — Anosike
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Chairman of Folio Media Group, owners of Daily Times of Nigeria, Fidelis Anosike, has described himself as a custodian of the newspaper, crediting its founding fathers and former leaders for building the institution into a major force in Nigeria’s history. Anosike spoke at the Daily Times Heroes Award in Lagos, where he said the newspaper’s legacy was built through the sacrifices and contributions of distinguished individuals, including Uncle Sam, Aremo Olusegun Osoba and Yemi Ogunbiyi. The event, themed ‘Honouring the Past, Shaping the Future’, brought together stakeholders to celebrate individuals who contributed to the growth and development of the newspaper. Anosike said Daily Times did not belong to him, stressing that his responsibility was to preserve its legacy and ensure its continued relevance. “When we talk about Daily Times, it doesn’t belong to me. Daily Times belongs to Uncle Sam, Osoba, Yemi Ogunbiyi, late Dele Cole and Chief Onyema Ugochukwu. They built Daily Times. “I’m just a custodian, and I’m one of the luckiest custodians you can ever find because all of them have rallied around us to make sure that we celebrate what we’re celebrating today and that we can actually shape the future,” he said. He noted that many of those who built the newspaper were in their 20s and 30s at the time, adding that their contributions extended beyond journalism to nation-building. Anosike also recalled that some former contributors and leaders of the newspaper went on to establish or strengthen other media organisations, citing Sam Amuka’s contribution to Vanguard. He said Daily Times played a significant role in shaping Nigeria’s national identity, arguing that its influence went beyond its status as a newspaper organisation. “Sometimes people think that Daily Times is a newspaper company. It started as a newspaper company, but Daily Times, the nation built it. Nigeria is not Nigeria today if there was no Daily Times,” he added. item.title: Security agencies rescue eight kidnap victims in Kaduna
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA – Security agencies, comprising the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Police Force and the Military, have rescued eight kidnap victims during coordinated operations in Kaduna State. The victims were rescued between October 31 and November 2, 2026, in intelligence-driven operations conducted in the Millennium City and Marabar Rido areas of Chikun Local Government Area, in collaboration with the Kaduna State Government. Addressing journalists at the DSS Command headquarters in Kaduna, the Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Rabiu, said the operations were part of sustained efforts to identify, disrupt and dismantle criminal networks responsible for repeated kidnappings in the areas. He said the communities had witnessed recurring abductions, raising concerns among residents and attracting public attention to the security situation. The rescued victims were identified as Jamila Muhammad, 27, wife of Abdulkadir Bello; Talatu Yakubu, 40; Yunana Bawa, 30; Calista Bishop, 27; Chidinma Onuwere, 36; Eucharia Obi, 41; Godiya Victor, 50; and an eight-year-old girl, Miracle Alex. The latest rescue came barely three weeks after security operatives freed Ahmad Zakka and members of his family from captivity on October 15, 2026. Rabiu said the successive operations demonstrated the determination of security agencies to secure the release of abducted persons and dismantle criminal networks operating across the state. He acknowledged the coordination provided by ONSA, the operational support of the Police, the intelligence contributions of the DSS and the involvement of the Military. The police commissioner also commended the Kaduna State Government, under Governor Uba Sani, for its cooperation and support in tackling kidnapping and banditry. He said the operations were in line with President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening national security and protecting lives and property through improved collaboration among security and intelligence agencies. Rabiu disclosed that security agencies were intensifying operations across the state, with additional personnel and equipment, including 30 operational vans and eight armoured personnel carriers, to be deployed to strengthen security and improve response to criminal activities. He noted that criminal groups often exploited the difficult terrain in parts of Kaduna State to launch attacks and evade security operatives. The commissioner urged residents to support security agencies by providing credible and actionable intelligence on the identities, activities and movements of suspected kidnappers and other criminal elements. He assured the public that information supplied would be treated confidentially and acted upon appropriately. Rabiu also called on traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to support efforts to tackle insecurity. He urged media organisations to maintain responsible and professional report

item.title: Soludo approves remodelling of Upper Iweka
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – The Anambra State Executive Council has approved the remodelling of Upper Iweka, Onitsha, as part of the state government’s urban regeneration programme. The project is expected to transform the aesthetics, functionality and land use of the area, a major gateway into Anambra State. The Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the weekly State Executive Council meeting at the Government House, Awka. He said the remodelling would cover parks and other public spaces, giving the area a new look in line with the state government’s vision of a livable and prosperous homeland. Mefor added that a detailed master plan and design for the project would be unveiled soon. At the meeting, the council also directed the Anambra Road Traffic Management Agency (ARTMA) to issue a one-month notice to owners of abandoned vehicles on roads across the state to remove them. The commissioner said vehicles not removed after the expiration of the notice would be impounded, taken away and scrapped by the government. He explained that the measure was intended to eliminate road hazards, improve traffic flow and enhance the safety and appearance of roads across the state. The council also approved the commencement of the selection, placement and training of the third batch of the One Youth, Two Skills entrepreneurship programme. Mefor said the Ministry of Youth Development would announce the eligibility requirements and application procedures in due course. He recalled that two batches of the programme had been completed, with more than 13,000 youths trained, empowered and mentored in over 60 skill areas. According to him, more than 5,000 beneficiaries have become millionaires and are now training and empowering other young people under the programme’s pay-it-forward model. “The One Youth, Two Skills initiative remains a flagship youth empowerment programme of the Soludo administration aimed at creating a new tribe of skilled, productive and self-reliant youths,” Mefor said. item.title: N70,000 transport allowance saga: PENGASSAN begs Ajaero, Osifo to sheathe swords, unite Labour
item.description: …Says rift not good for collective interests of workers By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo The Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, PENGASSAN, has called on the President of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and his counterpart in the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, Comrade Festus Osifo, to sheathe their swords and urgently resolve the differences between the two major labour centres in the interest of Nigerian workers. The appeal comes amid the lingering controversy between the NLC and TUC over the Federal Government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance, which the TUC leadership rejected. The disagreement has exposed differences between the two labour central organisations over the handling of the allowance, raising concerns about the ability of organised labour to sustain a common front in its engagements with the Federal Government. Agoro warned that the divisions could weaken labour’s collective bargaining power and undermine its responsibility to defend workers’ interests. The PENGASSAN President, who made the appeal at the Labour Writers Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) conference in Lagos, urged both leaders to prioritise dialogue, reconciliation and cooperation, insisting that the interests of Nigerian workers must take precedence over institutional disagreements. Speaking in his personal capacity, while also representing Osifo at the event, Agoro challenged the two labour leaders to practise the unity they had encouraged other labour organisations to embrace, stressing that the time had come for them to resolve their differences and present a common front in engagements with the government. He said: “I listened carefully to Comrade Joe Ajaero, and I want him and his twin brother to do the same thing that he advised Labour Correspondents Association of Nigeria, LACAN, and LAWAN to do. “We cannot shy away from the fact that things are not the way they are supposed to be with the two of them. So, in the same manner that you have advised both LACAN and LAWAN to come together without having to dissolve their centres and go for retreat, I think it is time we tell the two of them to pull back a bit and talk to themselves. “The reason why we have this platform is because we are representing the people (workers), and the interest of the people must be number one on our minds. Anything we are doing that will jeopardise what the people have put us in this position to do, we must move away from it. “We don’t normally come with problems alone; we always like to prepare solutions. I think it is time for both TUC and NLC to sit down and have a Memorandum of Understanding on how we want this relationship to work. “The Federal Government of Nigeria has married two wives, and if they think they have anything to gain by the discord between both labour centres, I think they are just joking. item.title: Nigerians have talent to lead World in sports – Shettima
item.description: —Tasks new CAF General Secretary with advancing African football, protecting Nigeria’s interests By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — THE Vice President Senator Kashim Shettima has said that Nigerians possess the talent and capacity to occupy leadership positions in global sports, describing the appointment of Mr Samson Adamu as the first Nigerian General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) as further evidence of the country’s potential for international leadership. The Vice President said Nigeria’s sporting achievements have been driven by the quality of its people, the dedication of sports administrators and the institutions that discover, nurture and project Nigerian talent onto the global stage. Speaking on Tuesday at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, while receiving the newly appointed CAF General Secretary and a delegation led by the Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Malam Shehu Dikko, VP Shettima congratulated Adamu on his appointment and charged him to distinguish himself through exemplary leadership and service to African football. “Our nation has earned its place in the world of sports. We have flown our flag in arenas where few expected us to perform magic and we have made the impossible appear almost familiar, fundamentally because of the quality of our people,” he said. Conveying President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s goodwill, the Vice President described Adamu as a role model for young Nigerians and urged him to approach his new responsibilities with diligence, integrity and a strong sense of national pride. “The President is proud of you Samson Adamu, Go and do a yo-man’s job. Go and promote, protect and project and preserve the interest of the Nigerian nation. So Samson I wish you all the best. “Football especially is a uniting force in this country. Anytime Nigeria plays, it tends to subsume all other identities. Football and sports generally is a source of unity for our country. What binds us together superseded whatever divides us,” he stated. He maintained that Nigeria’s diversity remains a source of strength, stressing that the country’s social and historical bonds are deeper than the divisions sometimes emphasised in public discourse. VP Shettima praised the often-unrecognised contributions of officials, coaches, talent scouts and administrators whose work provides the foundation for Nigeria’s sporting achievements. “The minds that organize, the hands that prepare and the institutions that give talents a fighting chance, are always not recognized. This is why from the bottom of my heart, on behalf of my Boss, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, we appreciate you,” he said. He recalled the contributions of Nigerian football legends, including Rashidi Yekini, Austin Jay-Jay Okocha and Finidi George, noting that their successes were made possible by individuals and institutions that identified and developed their abilities. item.title: ‎I’ll not let Senate, National Assembly down – DSP Barau pledges
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎The Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Barau I. Jibrin, has pledged to strengthen Nigeria’s democratic institutions and promote people-oriented legislation, assuring that he would not disappoint the Senate, National Assembly or Nigerians. ‎ ‎Barau made the pledge after the Senate Press Corps (SPC) named him the Most Outstanding Deputy President of the Senate Since 1999. ‎ ‎The award was presented on Monday at the National Assembly in Abuja in recognition of his contributions to legislative development, quality lawmaking, parliamentary leadership and effective representation. ‎ ‎Responding to the honour, Barau described the recognition as both an acknowledgement of his contributions to the legislature and a motivation to do more. ‎ ‎“This honour is not only an acknowledgement of the work we have done but also a motivation to do even more. As the popular saying goes, to whom much is given, much is expected. ‎ ‎“I assure you that I will not let you down. I will not let the Senate down; I will not let the National Assembly down, and I will not let the entire legislature or our country down,” he said. ‎ ‎The Deputy Senate President reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening democratic institutions, advancing people-oriented legislation and providing purposeful representation to the people of Kano North Senatorial District. ‎ ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Senate Press Corps, Comrade Taye Odewale, said the association’s assessment identified Barau as the most outstanding Deputy Senate President since the inception of the Fourth Republic in 1999. ‎ ‎Odewale, who has covered the Senate for 22 years, explained that the assessment considered legislative contributions, presiding capabilities, participation in debates, oversight functions, accessibility and commitment to humanity. ‎ ‎He disclosed that Barau had sponsored 48 bills within 40 months of the 10th National Assembly, with five already passed into law, despite the administrative demands of his office. ‎ ‎Among the landmark bills highlighted were the North-West Development Commission Establishment Bill, 2023; National Identity Management Commission Repeal and Enactment Bill, 2024; Agricultural Research Council Amendment Bill, 2024; Federal Medical Centre, Gwarzo, Kano State Establishment Bill, 2024; and Federal University of Science and Technology, Kabo Establishment Bill, 2025. ‎ ‎The Senate Press Corps also commended his constituency projects and empowerment programmes, which it said had benefited various groups across Kano North, Kano State, the North-West and Nigeria. ‎ The post ‎I’ll not let Senate, National Assembly down – DSP Barau pledges appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Minister tasks states, LGs on nomadic education funding
item.description: Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id-Ahmad, the Minister of State for Education, has urged states and local governments to prioritise nomadic and alternative education. She said they should give appropriate attention to the sub-sector in their education plans and budgets. Sa’id-Ahmad made the call on Tuesday in Kano while delivering a keynote address at an International Conference on Nomadic and Alternative Education Approaches in Africa. The minister was represented by the Vice-Chancellor, Federal University of Education, Zaria, Prof. Yahaya Bunkure. The theme of the conference is “Strengthening Inclusive and Flexible Education Pathways for Nomadic Pastoralists and Marginalised Learners in Africa”. The conference was organised by the Maryam Abacha American University of Nigeria (MAAUN), Kano, in collaboration with the Catholic University of East Africa (CUEA), Kenya, Capital University of Somalia and the University of Namibia. She said, “Sustainability remains one of the most important issues before us. Successful interventions must continue beyond individual projects and funding cycles. “Federal, state and local governments should give appropriate attention to nomadic and alternative education in their education plans and budgets. “Taking into account the needs of dispersed populations and resources required to maintain quality.” The minister urged universities in Africa to assist the system by evaluating the cost-effectiveness of different delivery models and identifying opportunities to use resources efficiently. According to her, establishing learning centres without providing trained teachers, instructional materials, supervision and maintenance will not produce lasting results. “Our deliberations should strengthen policy and institutional coordination, expand flexible and context-responsive learning models, establish stronger university partnerships, invest in teachers and learning resources,” she said. The minister said nomadic and alternative education must be recognised not as a marginal concern, but as an essential part of building a fair, inclusive and productive society. “Every child we reach expands the possibilities for that child’s future. “Every learner who acquires fundamental skills gains a stronger basis for further education, employment and participation in national development. “Every community whose children receive meaningful education opportunities gains greater capacity to contribute to Nigeria’s social and economic progress,” the minister added. The founder of MAAUN Group of Universities, Prof. Adamu Abubakar-Gwarzo, stressed the need for a new curriculum that would give nomads and pastoralists special consideration. He said that would enable them to become civilised and enhance their contribution to the development of their countries. item.title: Zamfara: Kaura wins fresh APC primary
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The ruling All Progressives Congress APC has returned a former senator, Yahaya Tijjani Kaura as its candidate for the Zamfara North Senatorial District, after he polled 16,758 votes in a fresh primary held on Monday in Gusau. The rerun followed a Court of Appeal judgment in Sokoto which nullified the party’s earlier primary for the district. The Returning Officer of the APC Senatorial Primary Election Committee, Alhaji Sani Abdullahi, declared Kaura the winner and certified the result. Abdullahi said Kaura met the requirements of the APC Constitution and Guidelines and secured the highest number of votes. Kaura, a chieftain of the party in Zamfara State, beat his closest rival, Sahabi Ya’u Alhaji, who scored 1,465 votes. A third aspirant, Sani Abdullahi Shinkafi, scored 1,447 votes. Kaura’s winning margin over the second-placed aspirant was 15,293 votes. The declaration formally makes Kaura the APC’s flag-bearer for the National Assembly seat in Zamfara North. The National Assembly elections are to hold simultaneously with the presidential election in January. The fresh primary was ordered after the Court of Appeal in Sokoto set aside the earlier exercise for gross non-compliance with the party’s guidelines and the Electoral Act. Justice Tunde Oyebamiji Awotoye, who delivered the ruling, upheld the earlier decision of the Federal High Court in Gusau. That court had voided the first primary in August 2026. The court held that the respondent, Hon. Abdullahi Shinkafi, proved his case beyond reasonable doubt. It also expressed strong reservations about how a senatorial district with 26,000 registered party members could return 70,000 votes for an aspirant. item.title: IGP pledges police readiness for 2027 general elections
item.description: The Inspector-General of Police (I-G), Mr Olatunji Disu, says the Nigeria Police Force is ready for for the successful conduct of the 2027 general elections. Disu gave this assurance on Tuesday in Abuja, when a delegation from the Special Representative of the Secretary General for the West Africa and Sahel paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja. The I-G told the delegation led by Dr Leonardo Simao that the Nigeria Police Force was adequately prepared for the elections. “As I speak with you, we have embarked on the training of our officers and have updated their knowledge about the elections “We have taken note of peculiar issues and that will be relating to the 2027 general elections. “In spite of the fact that the Nigeria Police Force is in charge of the internal security of the country and the elections, we know that we cannot do it alone. “We can only succeed with the assistance of our sister security agencies, so we have been having collaborative meetings, and trainings together,” he said. Disu said the force had held series of trainings with personnel of the Nigerian Army, Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, Customs, Immigration Service and the Department of State Services (DSS) in preparation for the election. He said the trainings also, involved how to include everybody in the election process, especially those living with disabilities. According to him, the officers have been trained to identify them, and know what to do when they see persons with disabilities. “So far so good, we are not afraid. We are confident that even if the elections start tomorrow, the Nigerian Police Force is ready to do what is expected of the force. “We are ever ready to go, and we want to assure you that Nigerians will not be disappointed with the activities of the Nigerian Police Force in the election,” he said. Earlier, the leader of delegation said there was always competition among political entities with emotions attached to it. He said such emotions could lead to violence if not controlled, adding that the violence had always been there in West Africa and Israel. “It is important, therefore, that all measures are taken to ensure that elections continue to be a political competition and not a danger to peace and stability of the country. “The police have a special responsibility in the preservation of peace and stability. “Therefore, we’d like to ask you to share with us, how do you see the country being prepared for elections, and in particular, your role?,” he said. item.title: 5 footballers who have been sent to prison over match-related incidents
item.description: Footballers who commit violent acts on the pitch can face more than sporting sanctions, with some prosecuted and sentenced to prison for assaults on fellow players and match officials. While football governing bodies routinely punish players for violent conduct through suspensions and fines, some incidents have attracted the attention of criminal courts, with players handed custodial sentences for assaults on opponents and match officials. Here are five footballers who have faced prison sentences over violent incidents during or around football matches. 1. Duncan Ferguson Offence: Headbutting an opponent. Sentence: Three months in prison. Year: 1995. Former Scotland international Duncan Ferguson was jailed in 1995 after headbutting Raith Rovers defender John McStay during a Scottish league match in April 1994. Ferguson, who was playing for Rangers at the time, left McStay with a cut lip following the assault. He was convicted of assault and sentenced to three months in prison after losing his appeal. He served 44 days at Barlinnie Prison in Glasgow before being released. He became the first professional footballer in Britain to receive a prison sentence for an offence committed on the pitch. 2. James Cotterill Offence: Punching an opposing player. Sentence: Four months in prison. Year: 2007. Former Barrow defender James Cotterill was sentenced to four months in prison after punching Bristol Rovers striker Sean Rigg during an FA Cup match in November 2006. The attack fractured Rigg’s jaw in two places, leaving him requiring surgery involving metal plates. Cotterill pleaded guilty to causing grievous bodily harm at Preston Crown Court. The judge said violence of that nature on the football field could not be tolerated and that a custodial sentence was inevitable. 3. Brandão Offence: Headbutting an opponent in a stadium tunnel. Sentence: One month in prison. Year: 2014. Brazilian striker Brandão was sentenced to prison after headbutting Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Thiago Motta following a French league match between PSG and Bastia in August 2014. Brandão, who was playing for Bastia, reportedly waited for Motta in the stadium tunnel after the match and struck him in the face, breaking his nose. A French court handed him a prison sentence, with reports stating he would spend at least a month behind bars. He also received a six-month football suspension. Although the assault happened in the tunnel rather than on the pitch, it arose directly from a match-related confrontation. 4. James Barnett Offence: Attacking a match referee. Sentence: 12 months in prison. Year: 2012. James Barnett, a 25-year-old footballer, was jailed for 12 months after attacking a referee following a six-a-side football match in Bracknell, England. Barnett reportedly became angry after being shown a red card during the game. After the match, he pushed and headbutted the referee before repeatedly kicking him while he was on the ground. item.title: Amnesty International demands release of detained El-Rufai supporter, Imran Usman Wakili
item.description: Amnesty International Nigeria has called on the Nigerian authorities to immediately and unconditionally release Imran Usman Wakili, who it said was detained over social media posts criticising the low turnout at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna State. The organisation made the demand in a post on its X platform on Tuesday, alleging that Wakili was also targeted because of his support for former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai. Amnesty International further claimed that El-Rufai had been unlawfully detained for more than 260 days. It described Wakili’s detention as arbitrary and a violation of due process, saying he was arrested after security operatives tracked him to his residence in an estate in Karu, on the outskirts of Abuja, on October 29. According to the organisation, a heavily armed team of policemen arrived at the estate at about 4.30 p.m. and asked security personnel to direct them to Wakili’s apartment. It alleged that after discovering he was not at home, the operatives arrested his younger brother, who lives with him, and the estate manager. The organisation said Wakili was at risk of ill-treatment, alleging that he had been denied access to his family and lawyer. It maintained that his detention was linked to his critical social media posts and argued that expressing opinions on matters of public interest was a fundamental right. “Detaining Imran Wakili solely for exercising his right to freedom of expression is unacceptable and shows contempt for the rule of law,” the organisation said. Amnesty International argued that under international human rights law, a social media post considered objectionable by public officials or other influential figures was not, in itself, sufficient justification for arbitrary detention. It urged the administration of President Bola Tinubu to end what it described as attacks on human rights and ensure Wakili’s immediate release. item.title: Tinubu’s reforms favour rich, worsen poverty — Atedo Peterside
item.description: Atedo Peterside, founder of Stanbic IBTC Bank Plc and Anap Foundation, has said President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms have benefited wealthy Nigerians while worsening the living conditions of millions of low-income earners. Peterside stated this on Monday during an interview on Arise Television, arguing that although upper-middle-class Nigerians had recorded improvements in their investments and incomes over the past three years, poorer households were struggling to afford basic necessities. He said the reforms had not adequately addressed the economic difficulties confronting the majority of Nigerians. “If you’re upper middle class, I can probably show on the blackboard investments in the stock exchange and all that stuff. “I can show on the blackboard that you’re probably better off in the last three years. If you’re a low-income worker, like somebody without much savings and struggling to eat — what 100 million Nigerians have to do, to eat two meals a day and struggling to pay your bills, I can show you that you’re a lot worse off,” he said. Peterside faulted the government for failing to establish adequate social safety nets for poor Nigerians while implementing the reforms. Citing 2025 data from TheCable Index, he said poverty levels varied significantly across the country’s geopolitical zones, with the North-West, North-East, North-Central and South-South bearing a heavy burden. He said only about 12 states and the Federal Capital Territory had poverty rates below 50 per cent. According to him, most of the states with poverty rates below that threshold were in the South-West, alongside Anambra in the South-East and Edo and Delta in the South-South. Peterside said the regional disparities could shape how Nigerians assess the impact of the government’s economic policies. He added that policymakers might not fully appreciate the depth of poverty in some parts of the country because they did not frequently visit affected communities. “High poverty in Nigeria is largely a zonal problem. It is a problem of the North-West, of the North-East, of the North-Central, and of the South-South,” he said. The businessman maintained that the absence of adequate social protection for vulnerable Nigerians remained a major gap in the implementation of the government’s economic reforms. item.title: Sultan a beacon of unity, stability, says Lawal
item.description: Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal has described the Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar III, as a unifying leader whose wisdom and steady leadership promote stability. Lawal stated this on Monday at the 13th Shaikh Usmanu Bin Fodiyo Week and the 20th anniversary of the Sultan’s coronation, held at the International Conference Centre, Sokoto. The event, themed, ‘Reviving Ethical Leadership and Social Harmony: Lessons from Sokoto Jihad Leaders’, attracted prominent personalities from Nigeria and beyond. In his goodwill message, the governor said the government and people of Zamfara State had drawn inspiration from the Sultan’s wisdom, guidance and leadership, particularly during challenging social and security situations. Lawal congratulated the Sultan on the 20th anniversary of his coronation, describing it as a historic milestone. He also expressed appreciation for the Sultan’s recent presence and support during the coronation and presentation of staff of office to 19 emirs in Gusau, saying it demonstrated his commitment to strengthening traditional institutions in the region. The governor said the legacy of the Sokoto Caliphate transcended geographical boundaries, noting that its values of knowledge, justice, moral discipline, responsible leadership and human dignity remained relevant to contemporary challenges. He urged Nigerians, particularly residents of Zamfara, to draw lessons from the teachings of Sheikh Usmanu Dan Fodiyo in addressing insecurity, poverty, moral decline and youth vulnerability. Lawal called for greater emphasis on peace, justice, education and social responsibility to strengthen communities. Earlier, the Sultan thanked individuals and groups who had supported him during his 20 years on the throne. item.title: Alli vows to surpass Makinde’s eight-year record in four years
item.description: APC candidate unveils ‘Oyo AHEAD’ development blueprint By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, has pledged to surpass the achievements of Governor Seyi Makinde’s eight-year administration within four years if elected in 2027. Alli made the promise on Tuesday during the unveiling of his manifesto, tagged ‘Oyo AHEAD’ (Itayo Oyo), at Theophilus Ogunlesi Hall, opposite the University College Hospital, Ibadan. He said the blueprint was designed to reposition the state through purposeful leadership, strategic planning, stronger institutions and people-oriented governance. The APC candidate said Oyo State had enormous economic and developmental potential that could be harnessed through deliberate policies and innovative approaches to improve the lives of residents. He said his ambition was to build a state where opportunities would be accessible to all, public institutions strengthened and the impact of government policies felt across communities, irrespective of their location or socio-economic circumstances. “Oyo State has enormous potential, but we must be deliberate, innovative and committed to translating that potential into tangible improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. Alli described Oyo AHEAD as more than a campaign slogan, saying it represented a comprehensive development agenda based on the expectations of residents and the need to accelerate the state’s development. “Oyo AHEAD is not just a campaign slogan; it represents a development agenda anchored on the people’s expectations and the urgent need to move our state forward. “We want an Oyo State that works for everyone, regardless of location, background or economic status,” he said. He said sustainable development required a coordinated strategy to strengthen institutions, stimulate productive sectors, expand economic opportunities and ensure inclusive participation in governance. “Sustainable development cannot be achieved through isolated interventions. We must strengthen our institutions, support productive sectors, create opportunities for our young people and ensure that every segment of society has a stake in the development process,” he added. The APC candidate said restoring Oyo State’s position among Nigeria’s leading states would require purposeful leadership, responsible governance and a development approach that placed residents’ welfare at the centre of government decisions. He said the manifesto contained policies, programmes and strategies to address the state’s development challenges across various sectors. Alli expressed confidence that his proposed four-year administration would deliver measurable results and surpass the achievements of the incumbent government over its eight-year tenure. item.title: Nigeria needs 10% growth to reduce poverty — Peterside
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Businessman and former Nigerian Stock Exchange chairman, Atedo Peterside, has said Nigeria’s economic growth rate of about four per cent is inadequate to generate the jobs and investment needed to lift citizens out of poverty, insisting that the country must target annual growth of 10 per cent. Peterside spoke on Tuesday at the second Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference in Abuja, where he identified declining investment, corruption, political patronage and the misuse of public resources as major obstacles to stronger economic growth. He said Nigeria’s investment-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) ratio had declined steadily since 1999, despite the optimism that followed the return to democratic rule, when local and foreign investors showed renewed interest in the economy. According to him, investors have been discouraged by an environment where access to opportunities is often determined by political connections, while small and medium-sized enterprises face harassment from regulatory authorities. Peterside called for an economy in which investors could operate without relying on political connections, stressing that public resources must be channelled into productive ventures to achieve the country’s growth ambitions. He warned against celebrating modest economic growth while corruption and the diversion of public funds persisted, arguing that procurement processes could be manipulated to enrich individuals at the expense of development. “Procurement can become legalised theft,” he said, citing inflated contracts and the award of projects to politically connected business partners as practices that undermine the effective use of public funds. Peterside maintained that Nigeria could not move from four per cent to 10 per cent growth without tackling corruption and ensuring that government resources were invested productively. Also speaking, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators but cautioned that headline growth figures did not necessarily reflect the welfare of Nigerians. Sanusi said the country’s economic growth of about 4.5 per cent represented progress compared with previous years, but argued that economic performance should be measured by its impact on people’s lives, rather than GDP figures alone. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. Sanusi questioned the significance of headline economic figures if poverty, unemployment and hardship remained widespread. item.title: Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, who contested the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District, has insisted that his mandate cannot be taken away from him. Kaura made the assertion while addressing a press conference at his residence in Kaura Namoda, where he claimed that he had been officially declared winner by members of the primary election committee sent by the APC national headquarters. He alleged that the committee’s chairman was taken to an undisclosed location by some individuals he described as anti-democratic elements. According to the senator, the chairman was abducted and subsequently announced a result declaring Senator Sahabi Ya’u winner, but a majority of the committee members rejected the announcement and jointly declared him winner. Kaura described the alleged abduction as an attempt to undermine democracy, insisting that the electorate would not accept such an outcome. He also dismissed the opposing camp’s claim that Sahabi had been declared winner, describing the announcement as invalid. The senator said APC members had turned out in large numbers to vote for him as the party’s candidate for Zamfara North in the 2027 general elections. He thanked the electorate for the confidence reposed in him and urged political stakeholders to respect what he described as the people’s mandate and the result announced by the committee members. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. item.title: High Court Hears Bid To Overturn Australia Social Media Ban
item.description: Australia’s landmark social media ban faces a legal test on Tuesday, as online platform Reddit urges the nation’s highest court to scrap the world-leading restrictions. Social media companies have been forced to purge millions of accounts after Australia banned under-16s from the likes of Facebook, TikTok and Reddit last December. The High Court of Australia will sit on Tuesday and Wednesday as Reddit, one of the most popular websites in the world, argues the laws are misguided and should be overturned. Reddit has highlighted a number of issues in its written submission to the court, pointing to problems enforcing the ban and a lack of scientific evidence about the harms of social media. “The evidence so far is that the effectiveness of the ban has been limited,” reads Reddit’s submission. Australia’s ban works by restricting children under 16 from holding accounts on the world’s biggest social media platforms. Map of Australia These platforms are responsible for weeding out underage users and face hefty fines if they are found to be falling short of their obligations. Reddit argued this approach was actually more dangerous, as registered accounts were governed by in-built safety features. Material posted on many online platforms and social media sites could still be accessed without an account, Reddit said. “Young people using other platforms without an account are also unable to be protected from exposure to particular harmful content as they previously had been,” its submission read. Australia said its restrictions would protect young users from graphic content, online predators and predatory algorithms designed to keep people scrolling. While there is a growing body of evidence about the harms of social media, Reddit argued there was no “scientific consensus”. Political discourse Reddit, which has also argued it should be exempt from the ban, said there was little research on whether certain platforms were safer than others. The High Court will also consider arguments from Australia’s Digital Freedom Project, which believes the ban restricts teens’ ability to take part in political discourse. “Social media is an important means of accessing news and engaging in political communication for young Australians, including children under 16,” the advocacy group argued in written submissions. “The restriction also risks removing beneficial sources of connection, support and participation,” it added. Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project separately announced last year they would challenge the ban. It was not clear how long it would take the high court to consider the case, although even the quickest decisions typically take months. Social media firms face mounting scrutiny over their use of allegedly addictive algorithms and stand accused of directing users to extreme content to keep them scrolling.
